review_notes: Reviewed all declarations and proofs in lines 1–119. The proposed replacement uses a standard nonnegativity criterion for zero sums; I checked its use in mathlib. No other proof simplification in the file was clearly easier to read as well as shorter.

findings.excerpt:
have hzero (i : κ) : trimWord (s i) = [] := by
    apply List.length_eq_zero_iff.mp
    exact Nat.eq_zero_of_le_zero (hm ▸ Finset.single_le_sum (f:=fun i => (trimWord (s i)).length) (fun _ _ => Nat.zero_le _) (Finset.mem_univ i))
findings.problem: The proof establishes that each natural-number summand vanishes by first bounding one summand by the total and then applying `Nat.eq_zero_of_le_zero`. This takes an indirect route when the total sum is already zero.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the body of `hzero` with:
```lean
  have hzero (i : κ) : trimWord (s i) = [] := by
    apply List.length_eq_zero_iff.mp
    exact (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg (fun _ _ => Nat.zero_le _)).mp hm i
      (Finset.mem_univ i)
```
findings.benefit: The replacement states the relevant idea directly: a zero sum of nonnegative lengths has every summand zero. The cited mathlib use follows the same criterion, so readers can recognize the argument without changing the mathematical content. The proposed replacement has not been compiled.
